solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ethnic non-religious art almost makes a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means the pieces are read from the far end towards the start

parts.note: laic means lay, belonging to the laity rather than the clergy

indicators.note: almost tells us to stop short of the end of the word art, dropping its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of art is dropped

explanation.surface: Secular art with an ethnic flavour is enjoying a revival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes a comeback' turns the whole run LAIC + AR backwards, giving RA + CIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe things relating to a people's descent or origin, so they are synonyms in ordinary use.

clue.text: Desiring relocation to the front row

indicators.note: relocation moves the letters of desiring to new positions

explanation.surface: Someone longs to be moved up to the front row of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringside seats are those right beside a boxing ring, the front row of the audience, so the phrase describes them.

clue.text: Finally, traffic congestion gets fixed by the authorities

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of traffic
fixed in the sense of rearranged or doctored, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Traffic jams are finally sorted out by the officials in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges C (the last letter of traffic) with CONGESTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognoscenti are experts or connoisseurs, people regarded as authorities in a field of knowledge.

clue.text: See 28
Prada chief and media agreed to remove clothing line …

indicators.note: chief means the head, the opening letter of Prada
removing clothing strips the outer letters off each of media and agreed

explanation.surface: The Prada boss and the press agree to drop a range of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Stripping media and agreed of their outer letters leaves EDI and GREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedigree is a line of ancestry or descent, especially recorded for animals.

clue.text: Wyatt carries noise reduction

parts.note: Wyatt Earp was the Wild West lawman of the OK Corral gunfight
lugs means carries something heavy

explanation.surface: A gunslinger named Wyatt carries something that cuts down noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Plugs worn in the ears are a device for cutting down the sound that reaches the wearer.

clue.text: Partly dressed blokes have time and money

parts.note: wearing only a vest, an undershirt, someone is partly dressed
blokes is British slang for men

explanation.surface: Half-dressed chaps have the leisure and the cash.
explanation.walkthrough: A vest is the British word for a sleeveless undershirt, so someone 'in vest' is only partly dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Money put into a business or asset in hope of profit is called an investment.

clue.text: Manage to escape rail workers' uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, a British rail workers' union

explanation.surface: Railway staff stage a revolt in order to break free.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a business is to manage it, a common synonym.

clue.text: Team's revenge here

definitions.meaning: a football or cricket side has this many players, so the number stands for a team
the word revenge appears in this puzzle at entry number 11, so 'here' points to that number

explanation.surface: A side looks for payback in this place.
explanation.definitionFit: Football and cricket sides field this number of players, and the grid places 'revenge' at entry eleven across.

clue.text: Shop corporation includes hotel for 7s

definitions.note: 7 down is RUN, so 7s are runs, a bout of diarrhoea; the plural slang names a single upset

indicators.note: includes means the shop word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a kind of shop
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
corporation is old jocular slang for a paunch or pot belly

explanation.surface: A shopping company takes on a hotel for its runs.
explanation.walkthrough: '7s' cross-refers to 7 down, RUN; 'the runs' is slang for diarrhoea.
explanation.definitionFit: This is jocular slang for the stomach upset travellers get in India, an attack of the runs.

clue.text: … close neckwear and lingerie …

parts.note: nigh means near or close
a tie is worn round the neck

explanation.surface: Continuing a list of a fashion line: close neckwear and underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is a garment of women's nightwear, which falls under lingerie.

clue.text: See 15
… so he could make footwear

indicators.note: the words so he could be made into something else by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Ending the fashion story: so he could produce shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A single item worn on the foot is one piece of footwear.

clue.text: Like Goliath, Matilda's good for Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner signals swapping the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: Tilly is a pet form of Matilda
fine means good

explanation.surface: Matilda is good, at least in the mouth of the famously muddled Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of 'Tilly's fine' gives 'Filly's tine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath was the giant of the Philistine people in the Bible, and the setter signs as Goliath.

clue.text: Hardware on entering in merry-go-round

indicators.note: entering means the small word goes inside the scrambled letters
round signals the letters going round into a new order

explanation.surface: Machinery parts going into a fairground carousel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'merry-go-round' splits: MERRY GO is fodder and 'round' the anagram signal, giving IRMONGERY; 'entering' puts the small word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironmongery is British for metal goods such as tools, locks and fittings, sold in a hardware shop.

clue.text: Suzanne met Meg overground 7s

definitions.note: 7 down is RUN, so 7s are the runs; the plural slang names a single upset

indicators.note: ground as in milled or crushed, so the letters are broken up and remixed

explanation.surface: Two women, Suzanne and Meg, meet on the surface rather than the Tube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overground' splits: OVER joins the fodder and 'ground' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for traveller's diarrhoea in Mexico, named after the Aztec emperor, an attack of the runs.

clue.text: Modify entrance to allow court admission

indicators.note: admission means one piece is let inside the other

parts.note: a door is an entrance

explanation.surface: Changing a gateway so that a courtroom can be entered.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor something is to alter or tamper with it, so it means modify.

clue.text: Criticises rival publication: a backward youngsters' pastime

indicators.note: backward means the whole string of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: pans means criticises harshly
a foe is an enemy or rival
mag is short for magazine, a publication

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a competitor's magazine, calling it a childish amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns all four pieces round as one string, which is why the final 'a' ends up at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Snap is a simple card game played by children, a classic pastime for the young.

clue.text: Time for breakfast

definitions.meaning: British slang for a prison sentence, as in doing time
an oat dish eaten in the morning

explanation.surface: It is the hour for the morning meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing porridge is British slang for serving prison time, and the oat dish is a breakfast staple.

clue.text: Applaud role reversal as drivel

parts.note: to clap is to applaud

indicators.note: reversal turns the role word round

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: Clapping when parts are swapped about is nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious nonsense, a synonym for drivel.

clue.text: Being smarmy and dysfunctional to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means only part of the word dysfunctional is used

explanation.surface: Someone is oily and somewhat broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Unction can mean an excessive, ingratiating earnestness of manner, so it is smarminess.

clue.text: Creature's backplate

indicators.note: back tells us to read the plate word from the end to the start

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer

explanation.surface: A beast's armoured shell on its back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backplate' splits: 'back' signals the turnaround and 'plate' gives LAMINA.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal is any living creature, so these are synonyms.

clue.text: Habeas corpus served with no- hopers round the counter

indicators.note: a writ is served, and here serving it up mixes its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A legal writ handed over, with hopeless types gathered round the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: A subtraction anagram: the letters of HABEAS CORPUS, minus those of HOPERS ('with no hopers'), rearrange to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads for counting, a counter in the sense of a calculating device.

clue.text: See 9
Like Ritz fashion in being extremely offensive

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters sit inside
extremely points to the outer letters of being
to fashion is to shape, so the letters are moulded anew

explanation.surface: Like the Ritz, fashion can be extremely in-your-face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' rearranges the two fodder words into LITZKRIE; 'in' sets that between B and G, the extremes of 'being'.
explanation.definitionFit: A blitzkrieg is an intense military attack, an offensive in the noun sense.

clue.text: See 17
Fool, on leaving Ulster, is still a fool

indicators.note: leaving means the Ulster letters depart from the fool word

parts.note: a nitwit is a fool
NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster

explanation.surface: A fool who quits Northern Ireland remains a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A twit is a silly or foolish person, a synonym for fool.

clue.text: Demanded medical treatment

indicators.note: treatment is applied to the word medical, working its letters over

explanation.surface: A patient insisted on medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: To claim something is to demand it as one's right, so the past tenses match.

clue.text: Furthermore, bet at a moderately slow pace

parts.note: and means furthermore, in addition
an ante is a stake put up in poker

explanation.surface: Also, wager on a fairly unhurried speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the musical tempo marking for a moderately slow, walking pace.

clue.text: First or second moo-kit

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
gear means kit, equipment

explanation.surface: A cow's sound as the first or second item in a kit.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom ratios on a gearbox, first and second, are the ones used for slow driving.

clue.text: Dodge observed as it speeds off

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dodge car is spotted as it races away.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep is to step aside to avoid something, so it means dodge.

clue.text: Don't go to bed with hero to crash into house party

indicators.note: the answer and hero crash together into one heap of letters that rearranges to the party phrase

explanation.surface: Stay awake so that a hero can gatecrash a party at home.
explanation.walkthrough: A subtraction anagram: the answer's letters plus HERO, crashing together, rearrange to HOUSE PARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain awake past bedtime is the imperative's opposite of retiring for the night.
